questions.scenario: The figure shows the CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) protein in a cell surface membrane. The diagram depicts a phospholipid bilayer with spheres for the heads and wavy tails. A membrane protein (CFTR) spans the bilayer. Its upper part has two branched chains of hexagonal units (carbohydrate chains) on the side above the membrane. Its lower part has large coiled loops in the space below the membrane.
questions.question: Describe the normal function of the CFTR protein.
marking_criteria: Explain the role of the CFTR protein in the cell surface membrane.
Mention the specific ions or molecules involved in the transport process.
hints: Stay focused on this: Describe the normal function of the CFTR protein — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Mention the specific or molecules involved in the transport.
questions.model_answer: The CFTR protein functions as a chloride ion channel in the cell surface membrane, allowing the movement of chloride ions across the membrane. This process is crucial for maintaining the balance of ions and water in the cell, which affects cellular processes such as the movement of water by osmosis.
questions.explanation: The CFTR protein is a type of ion channel that specifically allows chloride ions to pass through the cell membrane. Its role is vital for the proper functioning of cells, particularly in the regulation of water and ion balance.

questions.scenario: A genetically engineered crop has been developed to produce a specific protein that acts as a natural pesticide. The protein is produced within the plant cells and is secreted into the cell wall, where it provides protection against insect pests.
questions.question: Describe the role of the cell wall in the secretion of the pesticide protein.
marking_criteria: Describe the structure and function of the cell wall.
Explain how the cell wall facilitates the secretion of the pesticide protein.
Discuss the potential benefits and drawbacks of this genetically engineered crop.
hints: Stay focused on this: Describe the role of the cell wall in the secretion of the pesticide protein — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Discuss the benefits and of this.
questions.model_answer: The cell wall is a rigid structure that surrounds the cell membrane and provides support and protection to the plant cell. It is composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin, which form a complex network that allows for the secretion of proteins and other molecules into the extracellular space. In the case of the genetically engineered crop, the cell wall allows for the secretion of the pesticide protein into the cell wall, where it can provide protection against insect pests. This can be beneficial for reducing the use of chemical pesticides, but there may also be potential drawbacks such as the development of resistance in pests or unintended effects on non-target organisms.
questions.explanation: Describe the role of the cell wall in the secretion of the pesticide protein, considering its structure and function, and discuss the potential benefits and drawbacks of this genetically engineered crop.

questions.scenario: A genetically engineered crop has been developed to produce a specific protein that acts as a natural pesticide. The protein is produced within the plant cells and is secreted into the cell wall, where it provides protection against insect pests.
questions.question: Explain how the secretion of the pesticide protein into the cell wall can provide protection against insect pests.
marking_criteria: Explain the mechanism of action of the pesticide protein.
Describe how the secretion of the protein into the cell wall provides protection against insect pests.
Discuss the potential benefits and drawbacks of this genetically engineered crop.
hints: Answer every labelled part of the question, and link your points so a marker can follow the full argument.
questions.model_answer: The pesticide protein produced by the genetically engineered crop acts as a natural insecticide by interfering with the normal functioning of the insect pests. When the pests feed on the plant, they ingest the pesticide protein, which can disrupt their digestive system or interfere with their nervous system, leading to their death. The secretion of the protein into the cell wall allows it to be present in the plant tissue, providing protection against insect pests. This can be beneficial for reducing the use of chemical pesticides, but there may also be potential drawbacks such as the development of resistance in pests or unintended effects on non-target organisms.
questions.explanation: Explain how the secretion of the pesticide protein into the cell wall can provide protection against insect pests, considering the mode of action of the protein and its effects on pests.

questions.model_answer: The hydrophilic heads of the phospholipids interact with water, forming a barrier that separates the aqueous environments inside and outside the cell. This interaction helps maintain the integrity and fluidity of the cell membrane.
